01.event: Mar Ukva secretly tossed four dinars daily into a poor neighbor's doorway, and one day the poor man tried to catch the giver.
01.turn: The poor man chased them, and the couple fled into a still-hot furnace, scorching Mar Ukva's feet while his wife was unharmed.
01.outcome: His wife told him to rest his feet on hers, and when he was distraught she explained her giving was more immediate because she gave food at home.
01.summary: Mar Ukva daily slipped four dinars into a poor neighbor's door slot. One day the poor man went to see who his benefactor was, and Mar Ukva and his wife, who came together that day, ran from him into a furnace with banked embers. Mar Ukva's feet were burned, and his wife offered her unburned feet to rest on. When he was upset, she explained that her help was greater because she gave immediate food at home.

02.event: A woman from Mehoza married to a man of Neharde'a came before Rav Nahman, who recognized her accent.
02.turn: He first ruled by Babylonian custom, then the litigants objected that she was marrying into Neharde'a.
02.outcome: He reversed to rule that Neharde'a and its towns follow Shmuel.
02.summary: A woman from Mehoza, married to a man from Neharde'a, came before Rav Nahman about her marriage contract. He heard her accent and ruled that Babylonia follows Rav. When they objected that she was marrying into Neharde'a, he said that in that case Neharde'a and its towns follow Shmuel.
02.missing: What the exact dispute about her contract was is only in context.

03.actor: The sister of Rami bar Hama and her husband Rav Avya
03.event: Her marriage contract was lost and the couple asked Rav Yosef what to do.
03.turn: Rav Yosef cited the lenient view that a man may keep his wife for years without a contract, and Abaye objected that the law follows Rabbi Meir's stringency.
03.outcome: Rav Yosef conceded and said to go and write her a new contract.
03.summary: Rami bar Hama's sister, married to Rav Avya, lost her marriage contract, and the couple went to Rav Yosef. He first said the stringent view is Rabbi Meir's and the Rabbis allow years without a contract. Abaye objected that the law follows Rabbi Meir, so Rav Yosef told the husband to write her a new contract.

04.event: A marriage contract was brought before Rabbi Abbahu, with the scribe's handwriting and one witness's signature recognized.
04.turn: Rabbi Abbahu was ready to validate it, but Rabbi Yirmeya said the mishna requires the scribe to have signed.
04.outcome: The implication is that the contract is not validated on those grounds.
04.summary: A marriage contract came before Rabbi Abbahu, with the scribe's writing and one witness's signature recognized. He was inclined to accept it. Rabbi Yirmeya told him the mishna means the scribe must have signed as a witness, so the handwriting alone is not enough.
04.missing: The final decision is not explicitly stated.

05.actor: Rava and Rav Mari bar Rahel
05.event: Rava declared Rav Mari bar Rahel, son of a gentile father and Jewish mother, fit and appointed him an official in Babylonia.
05.turn: A verse seems to require officials to come from among 'your brethren', but Rava reasoned that a Jewish mother suffices.
05.summary: Rava ruled that Rav Mari bar Rahel, whose mother was Jewish and father a gentile, was fit and appointed him one of Babylonia's officials. Despite the verse limiting appointments to your brethren, Rava held that a Jewish mother makes him count as one.
05.missing: This is mainly a ruling with its justification; there is little scene or detail.

06.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
06.event: They planned to let a nursing mother remarry immediately, following a baraita.
06.turn: An old woman said Rav Nahman had forbidden it to her, and Rav Pappi cited a baraita of Rabbi Meir's decree.
06.outcome: They admitted they had forgotten the principle, and the halakha was fixed with distinctions.
06.summary: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to permit a woman to remarry quickly after her child was weaned or placed with a nurse. An old woman said Rav Nahman had forbidden it in her own case, and Rav Pappi showed them a baraita requiring a wait. They said they had forgotten, and the ruling was set with distinctions.
06.missing: Mostly legal argument; the narrative is thin and its end is a ruling.

07.actor: Rav Yehuda bar Yehezkel and Rav Nahman
07.event: A man from Neharde'a insulted Rav Yehuda at a Pumbedita butcher shop, so Rav Yehuda excommunicated him and declared him a slave, and the man summoned Rav Yehuda to Rav Nahman's court.
07.turn: At Rav Nahman's house, Rav Yehuda used Shmuel's teachings to rebuke every courtesy Rav Nahman offered, until Yalta urged her husband to end it.
07.outcome: Rav Nahman accepted the case, questioned Rav Yehuda, and the litigant's claim of Hasmonean descent was refuted by Rav Mattana's testimony of Shmuel; the man was publicized as a slave, marriage contracts were torn, and a mob chasing Rav Yehuda dropped its stones when he threatened to reveal their lineages.
07.summary: A man from Neharde'a insulted Rav Yehuda at a butcher shop and was excommunicated and declared a slave. He summoned Rav Yehuda to Rav Nahman's court, and Rav Yehuda went and used Shmuel's teachings to correct every courtesy and word Rav Nahman offered. Rav Nahman then heard the case, and Rav Mattana confirmed Rav Yehuda's claim that anyone claiming Hasmonean descent is a slave. Many marriages were annulled, and when a mob pursued Rav Yehuda to stone him, he threatened to reveal their lineages and they dropped their stones.

08.event: The two were walking along a road with a woman ahead of them.
08.turn: Rav told Rav Yehuda to hurry away from Gehenna, and Rav Yehuda pointed out Rav's own ruling that fit men may be secluded.
08.outcome: Rav explained he meant only men like Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi and his colleagues, so they must still avoid it.
08.summary: Rav and Rav Yehuda were walking and a woman walked ahead of them. Rav told Rav Yehuda to lift his feet away from Gehenna to avoid being secluded with her. Rav Yehuda reminded him that he had permitted this for fit men, and Rav replied that he meant only the likes of Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi and his colleagues, not them.

09.event: Ravina, sitting before Rav Ashi, saw a man tying his donkey to a tree on Shabbat and protested.
09.turn: The man ignored him, so Ravina asked Rav Ashi to have him excommunicated, then worried that he had acted disrespectfully before his teacher.
09.outcome: Rav Ashi reassured him that where God's name is desecrated, one does not defer to a teacher.
09.summary: Ravina was sitting before Rav Ashi when he saw a man tie his donkey to a tree on Shabbat. He called out to him but was ignored, and then said the man should be excommunicated. Afterward he asked whether this had seemed irreverent to Rav Ashi, who replied that when God's name is desecrated, no deference is owed to a teacher.

10.actor: A man who betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags, and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya
10.event: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya examined whether it was worth a peruta.
10.turn: The rule that betrothal depends on the item's value seemed to conflict with Shmuel's concern that it might be worth a peruta elsewhere.
10.outcome: The conflict is resolved by distinguishing certain from doubtful betrothal.
10.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a bundle of rags, and Rav Shimi bar Hiyya sat before Rav and checked whether it was worth a peruta. If it was, she was betrothed; if not, she was not. This is then reconciled with Shmuel's view by distinguishing certain from uncertain betrothal.
10.missing: What was decided about this particular woman is not stated.

12.event: They were walking on a road outside Eretz Yisrael and saw a man planting diverse seeds together, and another planting wheat and barley between grapevines.
12.turn: One suggested ostracizing the man each time, but the other said the law was not clear to him.
12.outcome: The other explained why the man's act was not clearly forbidden outside Eretz Yisrael, so no one was ostracized.
12.summary: Rav Hanan and Rav Anan were traveling when they saw a man sowing mixed seeds. One proposed ostracizing him, and the other told him he did not understand the law. They then saw another man sowing wheat and barley among vines, and the same suggestion drew the reply that by Rabbi Yoshiya's view this is not yet a violation.

14.actor: Rabbi Nehemya, Rava, and the poor men who came to them
14.event: A man seeking charity told Rabbi Nehemya he usually dined on fatty meat and aged wine, and Rabbi Nehemya invited him to eat lentils; another man told Rava he ate fattened hen and aged wine.
14.turn: The first man ate lentils and died; the second justified his food as coming from God, and just then Rava's sister arrived with a fattened hen and aged wine.
14.outcome: Rabbi Nehemya blamed the man for pampering himself, and Rava told the second man to arise and eat.
14.summary: A man asked Rabbi Nehemya for charity and said he normally ate fatty meat and aged wine. Rabbi Nehemya asked him to share lentils, and the man died from the plain food. Rava heard a similar claim from another man, who said his food came from God, and then Rava's sister arrived with a fattened hen and aged wine. Rava said he had been answered and told the man to eat.

15.actor: A woman who gave her property to her daughter, Rav Nahman, Rav Anan and Mar Ukva
15.event: A woman wrote a gift of her property to her daughter to keep it from her future husband, was later divorced, and came before Rav Nahman to reclaim it.
15.turn: Rav Nahman tore the document, Rav Anan complained to Mar Ukva, and Mar Ukva said Shmuel would tear such documents.
15.outcome: Rava questioned Rav Nahman, who explained that even for her daughter the woman had not wholeheartedly given up her own interests.
15.summary: A woman about to remarry wrote her property over to her daughter to keep it from her husband, and after she was divorced she wanted it back. Rav Nahman tore up the deed, and Rav Anan complained to Mar Ukva, who explained that Shmuel would tear such a document of evasion. Rava asked Rav Nahman his reason, and he said she would put her own interests before her daughter's.

16.actor: Residents of a crooked alleyway in Sura and Rav Hisda
16.event: The residents rolled up a mat and placed it at the turn of the alley to serve as a side post.
16.turn: Rav Hisda said this was not valid by either Rav or Shmuel since the wind throws it down.
16.outcome: The mat is declared ineffective unless pegged in.
16.summary: The residents of a crooked alley in Sura put a rolled mat at its turn to permit carrying. Rav Hisda said this satisfied neither Rav nor Shmuel, since the wind blows the mat over and it counts as nothing.
16.missing: The aftermath for the residents is not given; it is mostly a legal ruling on a case.

17.actor: Rav Yosef and two claimants holding deeds to the same field
17.event: Two deeds to the same property came before Rav Yosef, one dated the fifth of Nisan and the other only 'Nisan'.
17.turn: Rav Yosef awarded the property to the dated deed, and the other man protested, asked for a document, and was told a buyer could claim his deed was from the first of Nisan.
17.outcome: The remedy given is for the two to write authorizations for each other.
17.summary: Two deeds to the same field came before Rav Yosef, one dated the fifth of Nisan and the other just 'Nisan'. He awarded the field to the dated one. The other man protested and asked for a document allowing him to repossess from later buyers, and Rav Yosef said buyers could claim his deed dated from the first of Nisan. The solution was for each to write the other an authorization.

20.event: He went to learn Torah from Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua.
20.turn: Elazar's students ganged up on him like the roosters of Beit Bukya and would not let him study.
20.outcome: He learned only one teaching of Rabbi Eliezer, that one is liable to stoning for intercourse with a hermaphrodite as with a male.
20.summary: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi went to study with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua. The students there crowded in against him like fighting roosters and would not let him learn. All he managed to learn was one point of Rabbi Eliezer on stoning for intercourse with a hermaphrodite.
20.missing: The framing quotation of Rabbi Eliezer's ruling is mixed into the same segment.
